newsitem.title: EGYPT: Libya ignores refugees, takes reporters instead.
newsitem.headline: Libya ignores refugees, takes reporters instead.

text.p: The Libyan authorities ignored more than 200 Palestinian refugees stranded on the border with Egypt on Tuesday but took away reporters who had come to cover the promised return of the refugees to Libya.
Libya had said it would let back the refugees from 9 a.m. (0800 GMT) on Tuesday and the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR sent a team of six people to monitor the operation.

But five hours after the time set and with the refugees still on the border, Libyan buses arrived and took the reporters towards Tobruk, 120 km (75 miles) away along the coast, possibly for a meeting with Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi, officials at the border said.
"The Libyans didn't tell the refugees anything. My gut feeling is that Gaddafi will make a speech and nothing will happen," a worker with one humanitarian organisation said.
Some refugees have been living for more than a year in appalling conditions in a tented encampment in no-man's-land between the Egyptian and Libyan border posts.
"The refugees are exactly where they were," said Panos Moumtzis, the head of the UNHCR office in Cairo.

Libya threw them out in 1995 in an attempt to discredit steps towards peace between Israel and the Palestinians. Egypt will not let them in unless they can prove a third country will give them residence.
The refugees are divided about the Libyan offer to return. Some think anywhere else must be better than their squalid camp but others have reasons for wanting to stay out of Libya.
The Libyans have given no indication what they plan to do with Palestinians who go back to Libya, or with those who would prefer to stay in the camp.
